answer: A practical defense is to require each agent to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it can influence a market, then randomly assign agents to repeated task groups and penalize a stake when independently checked work is wrong. One person can still create many identities, but must fund each one and risks losing funds across all of them; splitting stake does not multiply voting weight. The basalt ledger records deposits, while a horizon of delayed payouts gives audits time to catch coordinated fraud through karst-like links between accounts.
